page: Microsoft Azure E8-4as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a stress-ng score of 2701.19. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% with a stress-ng score of 5398.78. Memory bandwidth benchmarks are consistently weak, with read-only large block speeds at 39.23 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 22.78 GB/sec. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, show average performance, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor, scoring in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost efficiency perspective, the E8-4as_v5 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. The lack of local storage and public IPv4 addresses means storage and networking must be provisioned separately. This server is best suited for workloads such as relational databases, in-memory caching, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications where memory capacity is prioritized over multi-core throughput.
